Your Brain

Oxford Read and Discover · Level 2 · Your Body · Pages 14–15

🔒 New Words 1 · Listen & Fill 2 · Write 3 · Present 4 · Mind Map

★ New Words

🔒 This part is for the teacher.

Teach these words before the listening task. Press 🔊 to hear the word (American English). Show the picture, read the meaning, then read the example.

brain

noun

The part inside your head that thinks.

“Your brain tells you what your eyes see.”

read

verb

To look at words and know them.

“Do you know how you read these words?”

touch

verb

To put your hand on something.

“Your brain tells you what you touch.”

write

verb

To make letters and words with a pen.

“Your brain helps you to write.”

speak

verb

To say words.

“Your brain helps you to speak.”

puzzle

noun

A game you think about to find the answer.

“Your brain helps you to do puzzles.”

amazing

adjective

Very, very good. Wow!

“Your brain is amazing!”

remember

verb

To keep something in your head.

“Your brain helps you to remember things.”

learn

verb

To get new things in your head.

“You learn things in the day.”

helmet

noun

A hard hat. It keeps your head safe.

“Wear a helmet when you ride a bicycle.”

2 Write a Summary

Write about your brain in your own words. Write 15 words or more. Then you can see my example.

💡 Answer these questions

  1. What does your brain tell you?
  2. What does your brain tell your muscles?
  3. What does your brain help you do?
  4. When does your brain work?
  5. What does your brain do at night?
  6. How can you protect your brain?

✏️ Start like this

  • My brain tells me …
  • It tells my muscles …
  • It helps me to …
  • My brain works …
  • At night, my brain …
  • When I ride a bicycle, I …
0 / 15 words

⭐ Example Summary

My brain tells me what my eyes see. It tells me what I see, hear, and touch. It tells my muscles when to move. It helps me to write, speak, draw, and do puzzles. My brain works all day and at night. At night it makes me breathe and makes my heart work. It helps me to remember things I learn. I wear a helmet when I ride a bicycle.

3 Presentation Script

Read the script. Practise it. Then present to your class!

Hello!Start

Good morning, everyone! My name is ________. Today I want to talk about my brain.

Look at this picture. This is a brain. It’s inside our head!

👉 Point to your head. Show the brain picture.
Part 1Brain tells

Do you know how we read words? Our brain tells us what our eyes see!

Our brain tells us what we see, hear, and touch.

👉 Point to your eyes, your ears, and your hands.
Part 2Move · Do

Our brain tells our muscles when to move.

It helps us to write, speak, draw, and do puzzles. Our brain is amazing!

👉 Pretend to write and draw.
Part 3Day · Night

Our brain works all day and at night when we sleep!

At night it makes us breathe, and it makes our heart work.

👉 Put your hands under your head like a pillow.
Part 4Remember

At night our brain helps us to remember things that we learn in the day.

Question for you: What did you learn today? (Wait for answers.)

👉 Ask the class. Say “Good job!”
Part 5Protect

How can we protect our brain? We wear a helmet when we ride a bicycle!

👉 Show the picture. Point to the helmet.
The EndFinish

Remember: our brain is amazing. Let’s protect it!

Thank you for listening! Do you have any questions?

👉 Smile and say “Thank you!”

🌟 Presentation Tips

  • Speak slowly and loudly.
  • Look at your friends, not only at the paper.
  • Point to the pictures when you talk.
  • Smile! 😊
